subject: Fysik
title: Magnetism and electromagnetism
sourceSummary: Magnetic poles and magnetic fields, the Earth's magnetic field and the compass, and how an electromagnet is built and strengthened. This also covers induction and the basics of how a generator and an electric motor work.
topics: the Earth's magnetic field and the compass

questions.prompt: What happens if you hold the north pole of one bar magnet against the north pole of another bar magnet?
questions.opener: Think about the basic rule for how magnetic poles behave towards each other.
choices: They are strongly attracted to each other
Nothing happens, poles only affect iron
They repel each other
One of the magnets loses its magnetism
questions.explanation: Like poles repel each other, unlike poles attract. So two north poles repel each other. Them being attracted to each other only applies if you turn one of the magnets around so that north pole meets south pole.

questions.prompt: How are the field lines of the magnetic field drawn outside a bar magnet?
questions.opener: Field lines have a definite direction, and it's determined by the magnet's poles.
choices: As arcs from the north pole around the magnet to the south pole, densest closest to the poles
As straight lines going straight out from the magnet's centre in all directions
As circles around the magnet's centre, with no direction
Just as a single line between the two poles
questions.explanation: Outside the magnet, the field lines go from the north pole to the south pole, and they are densest at the poles, where the field is strongest. The lines going straight out from the centre isn't correct — it's at the poles that the magnetism is strongest, not at the magnet's centre.

questions.topic: the Earth's magnetic field and the compass
questions.prompt: Why does the north end of a compass needle point towards north?
questions.opener: The compass needle is a small magnet, and it's affected by a much larger magnet.
choices: The needle is attracted to the pole star
The needle is made of a material that always points north
The Earth's rotation turns the needle northward
The Earth has a magnetic field with a magnetic south pole near the geographic north pole, and unlike poles attract each other
questions.explanation: The Earth acts like a gigantic magnet. Near the geographic north pole lies a magnetic south pole, and since unlike poles attract each other, the needle's north end is drawn there. The Earth's rotation has nothing to do with it — it's the magnetic field that controls the needle.

questions.prompt: You have an electromagnet made of copper wire wound around a nail. Which action makes the magnet stronger?
questions.opener: Think about what you can change in the coil without replacing the iron core itself.
choices: Straighten out the wire so it lies as a straight conductor
Increase the number of coil turns and increase the current through the wire
Replace the nail with a wooden stick
Turn the battery around so the current goes the other way
questions.explanation: The magnetic field in a coil becomes stronger when the number of turns increases, when the current increases, and when the coil has an iron core. Turning the battery around just swaps the positions of the north and south poles — the strength stays exactly the same.

questions.opener: Think about what happens in a coil when a magnetic field around it changes.
choices: That a voltage arises in a conductor when the magnetic field through it changes, for example when a magnet moves into a coil
That a magnet becomes warm when it lies near a wire
That a wire loses all its resistance in a magnetic field
That a magnet attracts copper and aluminium
questions.explanation: Induction means that a changing magnetic field creates a voltage in a conductor — if the magnet doesn't move, nothing happens; it's precisely the change that's required. Copper and aluminium also aren't magnetic, so the last option doesn't hold either.

questions.prompt: Which energy conversion happens in a generator?
questions.opener: Compare it with an electric motor — the generator does exactly the opposite.
choices: Electrical energy is converted into kinetic energy
Heat is converted directly into light
Kinetic energy is converted into electrical energy
Chemical energy is converted into electrical energy
questions.explanation: In a generator, a coil spins in a magnetic field, the magnetic field through the coil changes, and a voltage is induced — kinetic energy becomes electrical energy. The opposite, electrical energy to motion, is instead what an electric motor does, and chemical energy to electrical energy happens in a battery.

questions.prompt: An electromagnet has 50 coil turns and a current of 0.5 A. You rewind it to 100 turns and increase the current to 1.5 A. How many times stronger does the magnetic field become, if the strength depends on the number of turns times the current?
questions.opener: Calculate turns times current before and after, then compare the two numbers.
questions.answer: The magnetic field becomes 6 times stronger
steps: So the magnetic field becomes 6 times stronger — double the number of turns times three times the current.

questions.prompt: Summarise magnetism, electromagnets, induction, and how a generator and an electric motor work.
questions.opener: Start with the poles and the field, move on to the electromagnet, and finish with induction and the machines.
questions.answer: Magnet: always has a north pole and a south pole, you can never get just one pole · Pole rule: like poles repel, unlike poles attract · Magnetic field: the area around the magnet where the force is noticeable, drawn with field lines from north pole to south pole, densest and strongest at the poles · Magnetic materials: iron, cobalt and nickel — not copper, aluminium or plastic · The Earth's magnetic field: the Earth is like a giant magnet with a magnetic south pole near the geographic north pole, protects against charged particles from the sun · Compass: a small rotatable magnetic needle whose north end is drawn towards north · Electromagnet: current through a coil produces a magnetic field, strengthened by more turns, higher current and an iron core, can be switched off — used in relays, speakers and scrapyard magnets · Induction: a changing magnetic field through a coil produces an induced voltage, requires motion or alternating current · Generator: a coil spins in a magnetic field, kinetic energy to electrical energy, used in power stations · Electric motor: a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field is turned by magnetic forces, electrical energy to kinetic energy · Transformer: two coils around an iron core, changes an alternating voltage using induction.

questions.prompt: What happens if you hold the north pole of one magnet against the south pole of another magnet?
questions.opener: Think about the pole rule: like poles repel, unlike poles attract.
choices: They repel each other
They attract each other
Nothing happens
Both magnets lose their magnetism
questions.explanation: A north pole and a south pole are unlike poles and attract each other. Two north poles facing each other would instead repel.

questions.prompt: Which materials are attracted to a magnet?
questions.opener: Only a handful of metals are magnetic.
choices: Copper, aluminium and plastic
Iron, cobalt and nickel
Gold and silver
All metals
questions.explanation: Iron, cobalt and nickel are magnetic materials attracted to a magnet. Copper, aluminium, gold and silver are not magnetic, even though they are metals.

questions.topic: the Earth's magnetic field and the compass
questions.prompt: Roughly where is the Earth's magnetic south pole located?
questions.opener: Think about which pole attracts the north end of a compass needle.
choices: Near the equator
Near the geographic north pole
In the middle of the Earth's core, far from the surface
It doesn't exist, there is only a north pole
questions.explanation: The Earth's magnetic south pole is located near the geographic north pole, which is why the north end of a compass needle is drawn there — unlike poles attract. Like every magnet, the Earth has both a north and a south pole.

questions.prompt: What happens to an electromagnet's strength if you reduce the current through the coil but keep the number of turns the same?
questions.opener: The strength of the magnetic field depends on both the number of turns and the size of the current.
choices: It becomes stronger
It becomes weaker
It stays exactly the same
It swaps polarity
questions.explanation: The magnetic field becomes weaker if the current is reduced, since its strength depends on both the number of turns and the current. Swapping polarity would instead require reversing the direction of the current, not its size.

questions.prompt: What is required for a voltage to be induced in a coil?
questions.opener: Think about the difference between a stationary magnetic field and one that changes.
choices: A constant, unchanging magnetic field
A magnetic field that changes through the coil, for example through motion
The coil being made of plastic
The coil being completely still in a weak field
questions.explanation: Induction requires the magnetic field through the coil to change, for example by a magnet moving in or out. A constant field induces no voltage at all, no matter how strong it is.

questions.prompt: An electromagnet has 40 turns and a current of 2 A. You rewind it to 80 turns but reduce the current to 1 A. How does the strength of the magnetic field change, if the strength depends on the number of turns times the current?
questions.opener: Calculate turns times current before and after, then compare the two numbers.
questions.answer: The magnetic field is unchanged, just as strong as before.
steps: The magnetic field is therefore unchanged — the doubled number of turns exactly compensates for the halved current.

questions.prompt: What energy conversion takes place in an electric motor?
questions.opener: Compare with a generator — the electric motor does exactly the opposite.
choices: Kinetic energy to electrical energy
Electrical energy to kinetic energy
Chemical energy to electrical energy
Heat to light
questions.explanation: In an electric motor, a current-carrying coil is turned by magnetic forces, so electrical energy is converted into kinetic energy. The opposite, kinetic energy to electrical energy, is instead what a generator does.
